chunks: From him (Al-Shaykh), from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding the capital in which you engage in mudarabah (profit-sharing partnership), you are entitled to a share of the profit, and you bear no loss from the capital unless you violate the condition of the owner of the capital. Indeed, Al-Abbas was wealthy and would give men capital to work on as mudarabah, stipulating that they not settle in the bottom of a valley and not buy 'Dha Kabad' (a ratbah' (fresh dates with the kernel). If you violate anything of what I have commanded you, then you are liable/guarantor for the capital.

key_terms.الرِّبْح: Profit: The earnings generated from the partnership, shared according to agreement.
key_terms.الْوَضِيعَة: Capital/Loss: Refers to the principal amount or the loss of capital.
key_terms.ذَا كَبِد رَطْبَة: Dha Kabad Ratbah: Fresh dates with the kernel still inside, a specific commodity mentioned in the text.
key_terms.صَاحِب الْمَال: Capital Owner: The investor who provides the funds for the partnership.
key_terms.ضَامِن: Guarantor/Liable: The party responsible for covering the loss if conditions are violated.
key_terms.مُضَارَبَة: Mudarabah: A profit-sharing partnership where one party provides capital and the other provides labor.

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for liability in a mudarabah partnership according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *zikm al-khata’* (exemption from fault) in mudarabah, where the working partner retains profit rights without bearing capital loss unless a specific condition is breached. The example of Al-Abbas illustrates how explicit contractual stipulations, such as avoiding risky terrains or specific goods, transform the partnership from a pure profit-sharing model to one with guaranteed liability for the capital if those terms are violated. This underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on the autonomy of contractual conditions (*shurut*) in defining risk allocation.
